semantic_axes.description: Unformed content versus alternative specific readings

edges.boundary_rule: Nebulous describes an idea too vague or unformed to pin down; ambiguous describes wording or evidence that supports more than one distinct interpretation.
clues_a: no specific time, method or content
clues_b: two clear possible meanings of the same words
irrelevant_clues: long sentences, polished slides, confident delivery

misconceptions.M2: Calling two clear interpretations mere lack of detail

chains.frame: Which word best describes what Nabil communicates?

beats.text: Nabil's proposal promised to 'do something exciting with food someday' but identified no product or customers.
beats.decisive_clue: proposal lacked any concrete product or plan
beats.reason: The clue 'proposal lacked any concrete product or plan' points to indefinitely formed, not multiple interpretations.

beats.text: He made attractive slides yet still offered no actual business plan.
beats.decisive_clue: polished slides supplied no missing substance
beats.reason: The detail 'polished slides supplied no missing substance' leaves indefinitely formed as the better fit, not multiple interpretations.

chains.feedback_short: Polished slides supplied no missing substance; nebulous still fits best.
chains.feedback_deep: nebulous means vague, shapeless or insufficiently developed; ambiguous means capable of being understood in two or more ways. The first clue is "proposal lacked any concrete product or plan"; the next is "polished slides supplied no missing substance". Nebulous has no firm outline; ambiguous has competing readings.
